paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God doesn't ask for a Sabbath because He's picky about luggage. He asks because He wants His people to stop, listen and trust Him with the rest. The LORD says to keep the Sabbath day holy, and the command was never new, because He gave it to their forefathers too (Jeremiah 17:22).

The trouble was never that the command was hard to hear. The LORD says the forefathers "stiffened their necks and would not listen or receive My discipline" (Jeremiah 17:23). I think that's the part that should make us all sit up straight. I've got a bakery full of timers, and I still have to choose to stop and listen when God speaks.

Then comes the invitation tucked inside the warning. If they listen, the LORD promises kings on David's throne, a city inhabited forever and people streaming in with offerings for His house (Jeremiah 17:25-26). If they won't, He warns of an unquenchable fire in the gates (Jeremiah 17:27). So the question for you, baker, is simple: when God speaks, do you stop and listen? The Sabbath is a gift, and listening is how we take it.
